Detail: All cpp_*/cmake_* rules set required_tech explicitly on every rule; none of the four csharp_* rules (csharp_async_void.py, csharp_blocking_async.py, csharp_configure_await.py, csharp_disposable_no_using.py) do -- it silently defaults to [] in FieldRule. Inconsistent with the standard set out in docs/adding-language-support.md (always set required_tech explicitly). Low practical impact today since csharp-ast evidence can't exist without .cs files present, but it's a real deviation from the documented contract.

Concern: README nfr-review.yaml example references a tech key that doesn't exist
Detail: README.md's config example sets tech.cmake: true, implying a cmake tech key. No such key exists anywhere in detect.py's ALL_TECH_KEYS or _DETECTORS -- every CMake rule actually gates on required_tech: ["cpp"]. The example is stale/misleading and should be corrected or removed.

Concern: C++ test and fixture naming is inconsistent with other languages
Detail: Every other language follows test_<lang>_ast_collector.py / test_<lang>_deps_collector.py / test_<lang>_rules.py / test_<lang>_integration.py and tests/fixtures/<lang>-sample-repo/. C++ instead has test_cpp_ast.py (not test_cpp_ast_collector.py), plus 9 separate cmake-* fixture directories on top of 6 cpp-* ones -- a larger, more fragmented, less consistently-named surface than any other language.
